_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every upstream pin this repo depends on.
Nothing else in the tree may DECLARE a pin value. package.json and package-lock.json
files CONTAIN pin values, but they are derived: `tools/repin.py --check` fails if any of
them disagrees with this file, and `tools/repin.py --apply` rewrites them from it.
Prose that mentions a version must mention one of the versions declared here; the same
check enforces that, so a stale number in a README fails rather than misleads.
The re-pin POLICY (when to bump, what a bump must record) is PINS.md.

cpp.what: The C++ anchor. Base for every prepared upstream patch (M3, M4, M5, M9, M10), for the AVM_WASM build (M6), and for all reference material under reference/ except historical-protocol-specs/.

ts.identity: 4377ddf64c^ — the parent of 'refactor: remove the TS AVM simulator'
ts.what: The TypeScript anchor. The last commit at which yarn-project/simulator/src still contained the TS AVM and the public orchestration we reuse. Vendored into spike/src, diffsim/src and drift/src, and checked out as the worktree upstream/tsavm.

historical-protocol-specs.identity: 0285bb092b^ — the parent of 'chore(docs): Remove protocol specs from next'
historical-protocol-specs.what: The only commit at which docs/docs/protocol-specs/ still exists. Vendored into reference/historical-protocol-specs/. ABANDONED upstream on purpose; see reference/PROVENANCE.md before trusting anything from it.

trace_format.what: PAIRED WITH trace_format_nim BELOW; DD-7 says both branches are jointly required and neither is useful alone. The CodeTracer trace-format anchor, and the FIRST anchor here that is not aztec-packages. DD-7's Path A pure-Rust writer (CtfsTraceWriter) at the tip of the branch that builds it for wasm32-unknown-unknown and that exposes dropped_column_awareness(). RI-42's decision is `depend`, so nothing from this revision is vendored and PROVENANCE.md has no row for it: verification/build_ct_writer_wasm.sh materialises it out of the OBJECT STORE into ct-writer/build-wasm-deps/, which is a build input and is not tracked. A commit is pinned rather than a branch name followed, so the pin does not move when the branch does. PUBLISHED: origin/wasm/ctfs-writer at metacraft-labs/codetracer-trace-format has this commit as its tip. IT WAS NOT, WHEN M24 PINNED IT. The branch was local to one worktree on one machine, this file recorded that as the reason a commit is pinned rather than as a consequence, and the consequence is that `git archive` resolved here and would have failed in CI and in every other checkout while every M24 check stayed green. M24's review pushed the branch and made publication a CHECKED property: verify_ct_writer_wasm_zero_imports asserts this commit is reachable from a refs/remotes ref, with a negative control on the counter. Anyone adding a sixth anchor off an unpushed branch fails there. check_drift.sh still never visits this anchor: it resolves only the anchors the PROVENANCE mapping names, and it resolves them against the aztec-packages fork, which does not have this commit and never will.

trace_format_nim.what: THE READER, and it is a deliverable rather than a convenience. A wasm-produced Path A container cannot be read by stock ct-print: the Rust writer's zstd frames carry no pledged content size and the stock reader exits 1 with 'chunk compressed data extends beyond events.log'. The fix is one commit on this branch, baea074 'fix(reader): read an events.log written by the Rust CtfsTraceWriter', which adds decompressFrameOfUnknownSize. control_commit is baea074^ -- the SAME tree one commit earlier -- and verification/build_ct_print.sh builds BOTH out of the object store so 'this container needs that reader' is a measurement over a ONE-COMMIT difference rather than a claim. THE COMMIT PINNED IS THE FIX ITSELF AND NOT THE BRANCH TIP, deliberately: the tip is one commit further on (branch_tip_at_pin, 'accept a boolean value without the redundant text key'), pinning it would make the difference two commits, and a reader built at baea074 produces output BYTE-IDENTICAL to one built at the tip on M24's containers -- measured, which is why the smaller claim is the one made. Not vendored; PROVENANCE.md has no row. PUBLISHED: origin/wasm/nim-to-wasm at metacraft-labs/codetracer-trace-format-nim contains BOTH this commit and control_commit (its tip is branch_tip_at_pin). It was not when M24 pinned it -- see the trace_format anchor above for what that cost -- and test_ct_container_roundtrip_ct_print now asserts both commits are reachable from a refs/remotes ref.

_comment: Two @aztec/* nightly lines are in the tree at once, deliberately, and they are not
interchangeable. `current` is THE pin: new work uses it. `deletion_era` is frozen
evidence — the published line whose src/public tree is byte-comparable with the `ts`
anchor, which is what lets the deleted TS AVM run at all, and which still ships the
in-process NAPI AVM the differential oracle needs. Bumping `deletion_era` would destroy
the artefact rather than update it.

current.role: The pinned @aztec/* nightly. All new work uses this.

deletion_era.role: Frozen evidence. Do not bump; see PINS.md.

npm_exceptions._comment: @aztec-scoped packages that are NOT on the nightly line and must not be moved onto it. Each needs a reason; the check refuses any other exception.

@aztec/viem.why: A fork of viem republished under the @aztec scope, aliased in as `viem`. It follows viem's own versioning, not the monorepo nightly line, and no nightly of it exists.

@aztec/merkle-tree.why: The deleted TypeScript merkle trees (REUSE-INVENTORY.md RI-28). Upstream removed the package in e264dd4893 (2026-03-16), so this is the LAST nightly that ships it and no later one exists. Consumed only by probe-mt/, the probe that measured the undomained-hash defect. Pinning it forward is impossible, not merely undesirable.

npm_pin_witnesses._comment: Tracked files that carry an npm version literal as part of what they ARE, rather than as a dependency declaration. Two kinds. A MEASURED ARTEFACT records which pin it was produced against; if the literal drifts, the artefact has silently stopped describing the tree it was measured on. SOURCE THAT PUBLISHES THE PIN states it as behaviour: orchestration/src/disclosure.ts puts it in the runtime's own section-8.4 disclosure line, so a stale literal there is a false statement made to a user rather than a stale comment. Neither kind is a package file, so neither is a consumer. Each entry maps a tracked path to the npm pin its literal must equal. `tools/repin.py` and `verify_pinned_nightly_single_source` both allow these paths AND check the agreement; neither merely exempts them.

npm_consumers._comment: Which declared npm pin each package.json/package-lock.json tree must use. Every @aztec/* dependency in these trees is checked against it.

toolchain._comment: Not upstream-Aztec pins, but pinned all the same; recorded here so there is one place to look. The authoritative declaration for each is the file named.
